control: incomplete definition (CED LIM-2.A.2 requires three conditions: f(c) exists, the limit exists, AND the limit equals f(c). The equality is dropped here.)
title: Continuity at a point
body: A function f is continuous at x = c provided that f(c) exists and \lim_{x \to c} f(x) exists.
ced_evidence: LIM-2.A.2: "A function f is continuous at x = c provided that f(c) exists, lim f(x) exists, and lim f(x) = f(c)"

title: Intermediate Value Theorem
body: If f is a continuous function on the closed interval [a, b] and d is a number between f(a) and f(b), then there is at least one number c between a and b such that f(c) = d.

control: swapped definitions (a removable discontinuity is one where the limit exists and the point can be redefined, per LIM-2.C.1; differing one-sided limits is a jump discontinuity)
title: Types of discontinuities
body: The kinds of discontinuity a function may have at a point.

items.label: Removable discontinuity
items.meaning: the one-sided limits both exist but are not equal to each other

items.label: Jump discontinuity
items.meaning: the limit exists, so the function can be redefined at the point to make it continuous

items.label: Discontinuity due to a vertical asymptote
items.meaning: the function grows without bound near the point

control: hook expansion contradicts the CED (LIM-2.A.2's third condition is that the limit EQUALS f(c), not that f is differentiable at c). The entry is correct, so only the hook should be rejected.
title: Three conditions for continuity at a point
body: All three must hold for f to be continuous at x = c.

items.label: The limit exists
items.meaning: the limit of f(x) as x approaches c exists

items.label: They agree
items.meaning: the limit of f(x) as x approaches c equals f(c)

expands_to.means: the limit of f(x) as x approaches c exists

hooks.when_to_use: when checking continuity at a point
hooks.caution: State each condition in CED terms when justifying continuity.
